name: Abimael
overview: Abimael is a male figure identified in Scripture as the son of Joktan. Beyond this unique attribute, the biblical record does not provide further details about his tribe or additional personal notes. His mention is brief but establishes his place within the genealogical lines recorded in Genesis.
namesAndTitles: The name Abimael means '[my] father is God [El],' reflecting a theistic affirmation common in Hebrew names. This proper name, as recorded in Genesis 10:28, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a significant theological meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Abimael specifically as the son of Joktan, situating him within a known lineage. No other familial relationships are documented in the biblical text beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Abimael's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement as a descendant of Joktan, contributing to the broader understanding of post-Flood human lineage. His mention in Genesis 10:28 helps trace the expansion of nations and peoples as outlined in the Table of Nations, underscoring God's providential ordering of human history.
